diagnosed_skill_and_repair.overall_diagnosis: Across all three samples, the agent produced a structurally correct workbook but applied an incorrect volatility horizon scaling in the Reserves-at-Risk (RaR) calculation. It multiplied an already-3-month volatility (σ_3m, computed from monthly log returns over a 3-month window) by an extra √3, inflating Step 2 exposures and Step 3 RaR% by ~1.732×. Expected shock formula is Exposure = Reserves × Z(0.95=1.645) × σ_3m / 100, with no additional √T scaling since σ is already horizon-matched. The xlsx skill lacks domain-specific guidance on financial risk / VaR volatility horizon conventions, which is the root knowledge gap. A secondary concern (sample 1) is ensuring the 2025 gold price proxy is the simple average of Jan–Sep 2025 monthly prices mapped to the exact row range. A prior patch attempting to add this guidance was rejected (gate_no_improve), so the repair must be framed differently — more concise, worked-example-driven, and placed where the agent is likely to consult it.

skills.diagnosis: The xlsx skill provides generic spreadsheet formatting/formula-hygiene guidance but offers no domain guidance on financial risk calculations (RaR / VaR). The agent double-scaled a horizon-matched volatility by applying an extra √3 to a σ already measured over a 3-month window, producing exposures and RaR% ~√3 ≈ 1.732× too large (e.g., 7.10 vs. expected 4.11). The skill also gives no guidance on constructing a 2025 annual gold price proxy from partial-year (Jan–Sep) monthly data for countries missing from the Value sheet.
skills.repair_instruction: Add a concise 'Financial risk / VaR calculations' subsection under 'Financial models' in xlsx/SKILL.md with: (1) Horizon-matched volatility rule: if σ is already computed over the target horizon (e.g., σ_3m = stdev of the last 3 monthly log returns × 100, expressed in %), the one-sided 95% shock is Exposure = Value × 1.645 × σ / 100 — do NOT multiply by √T again. √T scaling is used ONLY to convert a shorter-horizon σ to a longer horizon (e.g., annualize monthly σ via ×√12). (2) RaR% = Exposure / Total Reserves × 100, using the un-scaled exposure. (3) Worked example contrasting correct vs. incorrect: Value=$7,471M, σ_3m=4.8133%, Z=1.645 → correct ≈ $591.6M; incorrect ×√3 ≈ $1,024.6M (~1.732× too large). (4) Drop countries lacking a 2025 Total Reserves value from the RaR table (no #N/A rows). (5) For countries in the Volume sheet but missing from the Value sheet, convert Volume → Value using the simple AVERAGE of Jan–Sep 2025 monthly PGOLD prices as the 2025 annual price proxy; verify the AVERAGE range maps exactly to the 9 Jan–Sep 2025 rows. To avoid the prior rejection pattern, place this guidance near the top of the Financial models section (not appended at end) and keep it under ~15 lines with the worked example front-and-center.
